style.vernacular: Low-rise Caribbean island town on a flat limestone island: single-storey and two-storey concrete-block houses and shops rendered and painted in whites and pastels, renovated West Indian-style cottages with pitched roofs and verandas, and a few stone-and-timber colonial survivals. Roofs are painted corrugated or sheet metal in red, green, blue or galvanized grey. Dry scrub, sea grape, coconut palms and sandy or coral-stone ground; very few buildings above three storeys.
style.ornament: Wooden fretwork and shutters on West Indian-style cottages, painted verandas, coral-stone and pebble work (St. Gerard's facade), bright painted fascia boards and shopfronts, louvred windows for ventilation.

sources.what: few colonial buildings survive; renovated West Indian-style cottages beside modernised shops; St. Gerard's pebble, stone, cement, wood and tile facade; flat site 9 m above sea level
18th-century coral-lime mortar, dressed stone and shingled hardwood-framed roof in the local colonial building tradition
